title: When the Day Draws to a Close
body:
Dear friend,

In Japan, December has a traditional name: Shiwasu. A familiar explanation of the name pictures Buddhist monks rushing from house to house to chant sutras as the year draws to an end.

Is the end of the year a busy season where you live, too? There is work left unfinished, and preparation for the year ahead. As soon as one task is done, another is waiting. Our lives pass in this hurry.

In seventh-century China, there lived a Buddhist monk named Shandao. Centuries later, Hōnen, the founder of Jōdo Shū, would look to him as his teacher. Among Shandao’s verses for worship is one recited at sunset, known as the Sunset Verse on Impermanence. Its opening lines read:

人間怱怱営衆務
不覚年命日夜去

We might put their meaning this way:

We hurry through our many tasks,
not noticing that our lives pass away, day and night.

More than a thousand years have passed. We can reach someone far away in an instant. Work that once took days can now be finished in a short time. Yet we are still busy. We are still saying, “Once this is done,” and hurrying toward the next thing. Shandao’s words speak to us as clearly as if they had been written today.

The work is finished, and another day comes to an end. But a day of our lives has passed, too. An unfinished task can be carried over into tomorrow. This day cannot come back.

At the end of the verse, Shandao urges us, while we are still healthy and strong, to encourage ourselves in practice and seek the Pure Land—the land of Amida Buddha, where we can be freed from suffering and continue toward awakening. Our lives are passing even as we tell ourselves, “Someday, when I have more time.”

This December, if you notice the evening light fading, take a moment to remember that you have lived this day. Then try saying Namu Amida Butsu—“I take refuge in Amida Buddha”—and turn your heart toward Amida.

Alongside the tasks that still await you, give some attention to the life you are living now. That is how I hope we might meet the end of this year.
